findings.reason: The protected Python solution reroots a binary tree with parent pointers using a target leaf node. It climbs the leaf-to-root path iteratively, moving any existing left child to right, setting left child to old parent, updating parent pointers, and clearing old child links. The solution runs in O(h) time and O(1) space; no candidate is required.
Iteratively climbing the path from leaf to root while caching grandparent pointers safely rewires parent-child links without losing ancestral references or introducing cycle bugs.

Traversing the h path nodes from leaf to root performs O(1) pointer updates per step, yielding O(h) total time. Auxiliary space is O(1) for scalar node pointers. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Accepts root and leaf Node objects, returning leaf as the new root of the rerooted binary tree with leaf.parent set to None.

The approach accurately details leaf-to-root upward path traversal, grandparent caching, left child rotation, parent pointer updates, old direction link clearing, and O(h) time / O(1) space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover recursive path reversal stack costs, repeated root search quadratic costs, link clearing omission risks, two-node tree limits, left/right branch leaf origins, off-path subtree preservation, left child displacement rules, and parent pointer agreement.

App Python and native Python solutions both execute the identical leaf-to-root path link rewiring algorithm with SHA-256 digests ee0dc25187bc78b2b97f1156e831eac427db612d2770172c38ebd6283d9821c6 and ade48ad7a36247ce6175dd5ec53597b5c74931d5eb7dfd1d2d20536653b85177.
